findings.title: Whitespace-tolerant classifier vs. non-tolerant numberedList/scan diverge
findings.problem: parseTemplateBody classifies with a whitespace-tolerant regex (/\{\{\s*([a-zA-Z0-9_]+)\s*\}\}/g) but the design's numberedList uses a non-tolerant /\{\{(\d+)\}\}/g. For a body like {{ 1 }} the classifier returns kind:numbered count:1 while numberedList is [], so no inputs render, variables=[] (length 0), and the send-core gate returns 400 for a template the user cannot fill. The design's claim that the counts 'agree' is false for whitespace-padded numeric tokens.
findings.fix: Build numberedList from a whitespace-tolerant numeric scan: [...new Set([...body.matchAll(/\{\{\s*(\d+)\s*\}\}/g)].map(m=>Number(m[1])))].sort((a,b)=>a-b), so numberedList.length always equals paramModel.count.

findings.title: Auth-template classification stated as 'typically numbered', not pinned
findings.where: Design 'Request body construction -> Auth templates' and 'Edge cases -> Auth template'
findings.problem: The send core guards category==='authentication' && !variables?.[0] BEFORE the body gate. If an auth template body classifies as named or none, the client sends namedParams/neither with no variables, so variables[0] is undefined and the core returns 400 'OTP code variable required'. FR1.5/AC11 require auth templates to behave as today (OTP is the first variable). The design only says 'typically numbered', leaving no rule for named/none auth bodies.
findings.fix: Pin the rule: for category==='authentication', force the numbered branch regardless of paramModel.kind, e.g. const effectiveKind = selectedTemplate?.category==='authentication' ? 'numbered' : paramModel.kind; and drive form/validation/request-body off effectiveKind so variables[0] is always populated.

findings.title: selectedTemplate possibly undefined inside per-recipient loop not addressed
findings.where: Design 'Request body construction' derivations inside handleSend
findings.problem: paramModel/isMediaHeader/headerKind/hasDynamicButton/numberedList derive from selectedTemplate which can be undefined (templates.find). handleSend early-returns on empty templateId but not on undefined selectedTemplate; derivations fall through to the none branch. Matches today's loose assumption, not a regression, but conflicts with the design's strict-typing posture.
findings.fix: Note that selectedTemplate is guaranteed defined when templateId is set (options come from the fetched approved list) and the none-default is a defensive no-op; optionally early-return if !selectedTemplate.

findings.title: Keep category typed as string (non-null) on the Template interface
findings.problem: Auth logic compares category === 'authentication'. category is always present on the full-row response. Confirming it must stay string, not be widened to string|null.
findings.fix: No change needed; keep category: string. Recorded so the implementer does not make it nullable.

findings.title: Preview header box wording slightly overstates media-only
findings.problem: The real preview box renders for any headerType !== 'none' and prints 'Text Header' for text headers and 'Media' for image/video/document. The design's parenthetical implies it prints 'Media' for the media types only, which is accurate but could read as media-only. AC8 (indicate a media header) is satisfied either way.
findings.fix: Reword to: the existing header box renders for any non-none header, printing 'Media' for image/video/document and 'Text Header' for text; the media case satisfies AC8. No code change.

findings.title: Confirm session vs public success-shape divergence is intentional
findings.where: Design 'Route design -> Unchanged and explicitly preserved'
findings.problem: Session route returns { id, status:'sent', message:'...' } (string message) while the public route returns { id, status, metaMessageId }. The design correctly preserves the session shape; recorded to confirm no accidental drift toward the public shape.
